steps.text: Heat the oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium. Add the potatoes and onion with a pinch of the salt and cook gently, stirring now and then, for 15 minutes - a knife should slide through a potato slice with no resistance.
Pour everything into a sieve set over a bowl and let it drain for 5 minutes; keep 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the remaining salt in a large bowl, then fold the warm potatoes through so every slice coats.
Let the mixture sit for 10 minutes - the potatoes drink some egg and the wedges hold together better.
Wipe the skillet, add the reserved oil, and set it over medium. Pour in the egg mixture and smooth the top.
Cook for 5 minutes, drawing the edges in with a spatula once or twice, until the bottom is deep brown and the top is barely wet.
Slide the tortilla onto a plate, set the pan over it, and flip both together in one confident motion; slide it back in to cook the soft side for 3 minutes.
An egg dish is safe at 160°F (71°C) - check the center with a thermometer; the middle should be just set and still tender.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Rest the tortilla for 10 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature, cut into wedges. It keeps three days chilled and eats well cold.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
